how_to_use: Each item is a proposal, not a change. Nothing in this list has been implemented beyond what the 'already_shipped' set describes. Mark a decision in DECIDED below and the next build renders the outcome.
already_shipped: Disclosure strip under the masthead on every page, repeated in the footer (R01–R03, R12).
No prices and no star ratings anywhere on the site (R04, R05).
Buy buttons refuse to render without tag=shopnow047c-20 (R06).
Flagged for Review page with seven items and source links.
Open-questions register with an owner and a resolution method per question.
Five-event, cookie-free analytics script with an endpoint you configure.
Build-time link and price-pattern checks that fail CI.

suggestions.title: Make the front page a front page, not a verification report
suggestions.problem: The register was the most interesting thing on the page. A shopper does not arrive wanting to read a source register.
suggestions.proposal: Lead with three shape-based picks — dual basket, single basket, oven — each with one sentence of who it suits. Move the register, the dashboard, and the compliance record into a single footer group where they stay reachable but never compete with the products.
suggestions.tradeoff: You lose the 'we verified everything' impression on first paint. You gain a page a buyer can act on in ten seconds.
suggestions.decision_needed: None — shipped in this build. Flag it if you want the register back above the fold.

suggestions.title: Split the catalog by shape, not by brand
suggestions.problem: Four of five links are air fryers, two of those are the same brand. Brand-led navigation makes the choice look arbitrary.
suggestions.proposal: Three category pages: Air fryers, Air fryer ovens, Thermometers. Within air fryers, the reviewer chooses by basket shape first, brand second.
suggestions.tradeoff: Brand searches convert well if you have brand authority. You do not yet. Shape is the buyer's first real question.

suggestions.title: Publish four question-shaped guides before any product roundup
suggestions.problem: A roundup titled 'best air fryer' competes with a thousand established sites. A question-shaped guide can win a query no one has answered well.
suggestions.proposal: Write: 'Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?', 'A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity', 'How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs', and 'Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance.' Each one is answerable from the verified specs already in the register.
suggestions.tradeoff: These titles carry no search-volume claim. They are editorial hypotheses. If Search Console shows no impressions after 60 days, retire the format rather than the topic.
suggestions.decision_needed: Approve the four working titles, or name the four you would rather have.
suggestions.note: These are working titles, not claims about popularity, search volume, or product superiority.
suggestions.shipped: Two of the four are live as drafts on this site with the verified spec tables behind them.

suggestions.title: Replace the two 'winner' badges with a fit statement
suggestions.problem: 'Best overall' implies a ranking you cannot substantiate without hands-on testing, and it is the fastest way to sound like every other affiliate page.
suggestions.proposal: Instead of a badge, each card states a fit condition: 'Pick this if two foods need different temperatures.' It is falsifiable, it is useful, and it does not require a lab.
suggestions.tradeoff: Badges scan faster than sentences and may lift click-through in the short term. They also invite the exact scrutiny you cannot yet survive.
suggestions.decision_needed: Choose badge, fit statement, or both.

suggestions.title: Add a counter-depth and cabinet-clearance checker
suggestions.problem: The most common reason an air fryer gets returned is that it does not fit where the buyer planned to put it. Depth and height are already verified for four products.
suggestions.proposal: A single input pair — available depth, available height — that filters the cards to the models that clear it. Pure client-side arithmetic on values already sourced to manufacturer pages.
suggestions.tradeoff: Adds a step before the reader sees products. Solved by defaulting the checker to open, not blocking.
suggestions.decision_needed: Approve the interaction. No new data is required.

suggestions.title: State the 212 F probe limit as the lead qualifier on the thermometer page
suggestions.problem: Buyers assume a 1,000 F thermometer measures 1,000 F oil. The inserted portion is rated to 212 F; the 1,000 F figure is the ambient sensor.
suggestions.proposal: Put that distinction in the second sentence, not the footnote. It is the single most useful thing on the page and nobody else states it plainly.
suggestions.tradeoff: It may read as a reason not to buy. It is also the reason a reader will trust the next page they read here.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm the wording is not read as a defect claim. It is a specification, not a fault.

suggestions.title: Give every outbound link a visible product-intent record
suggestions.problem: You cannot prove what a submitted link was supposed to point to once it is live.
suggestions.proposal: For each submitted link store the intended ASIN, the official listing URL, the confirmation date, and the source. Keep the observed redirect target in a separate field. Never merge them.
suggestions.tradeoff: Two fields to maintain per link. That is the point: the intended target and the observed target are different claims and must be able to disagree in public.
suggestions.decision_needed: None — the schema is live in data/products.json and rendered on each review page.

suggestions.title: Test one Special Link before scaling to five
suggestions.problem: The supplied links carry no tag. Building a five-product site on untagged links would create traffic that earns nothing and a tracking record that proves nothing.
suggestions.proposal: Re-issue one link from Associates Central SiteStripe with tag=shopnow047c-20. Click it yourself. Confirm the click appears in the Associates report against that tag. Only then re-issue the other four.
suggestions.tradeoff: Delays launch by days. Launching on untagged links costs every click in the meantime and teaches you nothing.
suggestions.blocked_by: FLG-003. Needs the account holder to open Associates Central.
suggestions.decision_needed: Do the one-link test now, or accept zero measurable traffic until it is done.

suggestions.title: Publish a correction log and keep it public
suggestions.problem: When two official pages disagree, most affiliate sites pick the friendlier number and move on. That is how a site becomes untrustworthy one spec at a time.
suggestions.proposal: A dated list of every correction and every unresolved conflict, linked from the footer. FLG-001 through FLG-007 become the first seven entries.
suggestions.tradeoff: It makes your uncertainty legible. It also makes it auditable, which is the only durable advantage a small site has.
suggestions.decision_needed: Approve a public correction log, or keep the flag page internal-only.

suggestions.title: Write for one person: the renter with 15 inches of counter
suggestions.problem: 'Everyone who cooks' is not an audience. Four of the five products are countertop appliances whose main constraint is space.
suggestions.proposal: Pick one reader and hold the line: someone with limited counter depth, cooking for two to four, who wants one appliance to do more than one job. Every guide answers a question that reader has.
suggestions.tradeoff: You give up the family-of-six and the outdoor-smoker reader. Both are better served by sites that already own those queries.
suggestions.decision_needed: Name the reader, or name a different one. This single decision changes all copy.

suggestions.title: Publish on a cadence you can defend: one guide every two weeks
suggestions.problem: A burst of twelve pages then silence is the signature of a generated site. Search engines and readers both read cadence as a signal.
suggestions.proposal: One guide every two weeks, each added to sitemap.xml and feed.xml in the same commit. After 60 days, choose the next topic from Search Console impressions rather than instinct.
suggestions.tradeoff: Slower than a content dump. Twelve weeks gives you six honest pages and real query data.
suggestions.decision_needed: Commit to the cadence, or set a different one. Do not leave it implicit.

suggestions.title: Put the comparison table behind a 'what actually differs' column
suggestions.problem: Spec tables list everything equally. A buyer needs the two rows that change the decision.
suggestions.proposal: Every product table carries a final column that names the one spec that makes this model the wrong choice for someone. On P3 it is 400 F versus 450 F. On P1 it is 3 quarts per basket.
suggestions.tradeoff: Some rows will read as negative. They are the reason the table gets read.

suggestions.title: Do not build an AI content pipeline until three human-edited guides exist
suggestions.problem: The brief asks for automated article generation. Automating before the editorial standard exists produces volume with no standard, which is the failure mode you asked to avoid.
suggestions.proposal: Write and hand-edit three guides. Note every judgment call. Those notes become the checklist a generator would have to satisfy. Only then decide whether to automate drafting, and keep a human gate before publish.
suggestions.tradeoff: Slower to volume. The alternative is scaling a voice nobody chose.
suggestions.decision_needed: Agree to the sequence, or accept that automated drafts ship unreviewed.

suggestions.title: Keep the analytics endpoint off until someone owns the data
suggestions.problem: A counter with no owner accumulates data nobody reads and a retention question nobody answers.
suggestions.proposal: Ship the script with the endpoint unset so it fails open and records nothing. Turn it on when a named person will read the dashboard monthly and can answer how long events are kept.
suggestions.tradeoff: You launch without traffic numbers. Given FLG-003, the numbers would be meaningless anyway.
suggestions.decision_needed: Name the endpoint owner and a retention period.

suggestions.title: Reader polish: one brand, and imagery that is what it says it is
suggestions.problem: This publication ships as 'Countertop & Co.' while the root site ships as 'Affil3', and it uses editorial illustrations rather than product photography because marketplace images are Program Content and no original shots exist.
suggestions.proposal: Choose one name and one domain, and commission original photography of units you own. Until then keep the illustrations labelled, which is what they already are.
suggestions.tradeoff: A single name and real photographs are the cheapest trust win available, and both need something a build cannot supply: a decision and a camera.
suggestions.decision_needed: Pick the name, or keep both and say so on the About page.

suggestions.title: Reader polish: a name and a check date on every page
suggestions.problem: Guides carry a team byline. A specification-check date is already printed next to every table, which is the harder half of an authorship signal.
suggestions.proposal: Add one named editor with a short bio and a corrections address. The method does not change; only the name above it does.
suggestions.tradeoff: A named person has to answer for corrections. That is the point, and it is also the cost.
suggestions.decision_needed: Name the editor, or confirm the team byline is permanent.

suggestions.title: Reader polish: verify Search Console and pick the next guide from the query report
suggestions.problem: Canonical URLs, JSON-LD, sitemap.xml and the RSS feed all ship. Search Console does not, so nobody can see which guides are found.
suggestions.proposal: Verify the property, submit the sitemap, and read the Performance report before writing the next guide.
suggestions.tradeoff: Needs an owner Google account and an hour. It is the only remaining decision that turns topic choice from instinct into evidence.
suggestions.decision_needed: Verify the property, or accept that cadence is chosen blind.

suggestions.title: Reader polish: RSS now, email only when there is something to send
suggestions.problem: An email form or a seasonal hub added before there is query data asks readers for an address with nothing behind it, and email brings its own rules: the Amazon Trademark Guidelines govern marks and links in email.
suggestions.proposal: Keep RSS as the only subscription route until at least three guides exist and the email rules have been read.
suggestions.tradeoff: No direct channel to readers, and no consent or retention obligations either.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm RSS-only, or scope the email list and the email-rules review together.
